home.leadIn: Every strategy here is a set of rules, written out in full:
home.leadOut: No code. Nothing hidden. If you can read it, you can decide whether you trust it.

drawdown.label: Worst fall from its own peak
drawdown.untestedHelp: This strategy has no backtest on record. Nothing is known about how it behaved.

backtest.heading: Test this strategy
backtest.intro: The rules are run over past price data. What comes out is a measurement of what happened, not a prediction.
backtest.fixtureNote: These settings are fixed. Unless every strategy is measured with the same capital, the results cannot be compared.
backtest.again: Test again over a different period
backtest.runningHelp: Candle data is being downloaded and the rules are being run. This can take a few minutes; the page updates itself.
backtest.failedHelp: The container did not run, or the data could not be fetched. The output below says what happened.
backtest.noTradesHelp: The rules produced no signal over this period. There is nothing to measure — this does not make the strategy bad; it means its conditions never occurred in the period you chose.

measurement.heading: Measurement
measurement.marketChange: The market over the same period
measurement.profitFactorHelp: What it won divided by what it lost. Below 1 means the losses outweighed the gains.
measurement.maxDrawdownHelp: How far the strategy fell from its own peak. This is the number you have to sit through.
measurement.winRateHelp: On its own this says nothing. Read it after the three numbers above.
measurement.consecutiveLosses: {count, plural, one {# loss in a row at worst} other {# losses in a row at worst}}

disclaimer.heading: Before you read the numbers
disclaimer.winRate: A strategy can win 82% of its trades and still lose money. In this project's own testing, one did: small wins taken at 1–4%, losses left to run to 10%.
disclaimer.backtest: A backtest shows how a rule would have done on data it was chosen against. It is not a prediction.
disclaimer.risk: Trading carries real risk of loss. Paper trading is the default. Stay there until you understand what a strategy does.

run.heading: Run this strategy
run.intro: The rules run on paper against live prices. No real money is used.
run.unmeasured: This strategy has no measurement. Nothing is known about how it behaved — testing it first is the safer order.
run.sameSetup: Exactly the setup it was measured with: {count} major pairs · {exchange} · {wallet} {currency} paper wallet
run.existing: {count, plural, one {# bot already runs this strategy} other {# bots already run this strategy}}

bots.heading: Bots
bots.emptyHelp: Open a strategy and run it to start. Bots trade on paper; no real money is used.
bots.outdated: A newer version is in the catalog. This bot runs v{version} and will keep doing so.
bots.setup: {count} pairs · {exchange} · {stake} {currency} per trade · at most {max} open
bots.removeHelp: The container and the bot's files are deleted. Closed trades are kept.
bots.closeHelp: The position is closed at the market price and the profit or loss becomes final.
bots.startingHelp: The bot is starting. Freqtrade is loading exchange markets; this can take half a minute.
bots.noEvents: This bot has never gone down on its own.

editor.forkHeading: Make your own from this one
editor.forkNote: Strategies that ship with the repository are never changed. Saving creates your own copy; the original stays as it is.
editor.versionNote: Saving creates v{next}. v{current} is not deleted — bots running it are unaffected.
editor.name: Strategy name
editor.previewHelp: These sentences are generated from the rules themselves — the same text you will see in the catalog.
editor.invalid: The ruleset is not valid yet:
editor.notEditable: This strategy cannot be opened in the form
editor.notEditableNested: It contains nested conditions. The form handles one level: comparisons joined by "all" or "any".
editor.notEditableNegated: It contains a negated condition, which the form cannot express.
editor.notEditableBare: It has an unexpected condition shape.
editor.archiveHelp: It leaves the catalog. Its measurements and any bots running it stay; nothing is deleted.
